episodes.180813: Showers and storms across East-Central Nevada produced gusty thunderstorm winds.
episodes.180830: A line of showers and thunderstorms crossed central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of July 17, 2023. One cell in this line produced sporadic wind damage from Perry County into upper Dauphin County.
episodes.180856: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.180901: Numerous to widespread strong and severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon amid a favorable environment of up to 3000 J/kg of CAPE and 30 knots of deep shear, while lift was initiated by an upper wave and associated low-level boundary across northern central Indiana.  Scattered large hail was focused over the western and northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro and near Bloomington.  Several storms produced damaging winds near the Interstate 69 corridor, and eventually in southeastern central Indiana as the episode continued into the evening.  Greatest damage ranged from several trees downed in both southeastern Hamilton County and Jackson County to damaged orchard crops amid several reports of up to 2.00 inch hail in Hendricks County.
episodes.181211: Preexisting hot and muggy conditions contributed to unsettled weather in West Virginia on both July 17th and 18th. Each afternoon observed strong to severe thunderstorms sprouting during peak heating hours, with damaging winds and a few instances of hails accompanying convection. Tree damage was the primary result of the passing storms, especially across portions of central and southern West Virginia.
episodes.181261: Unsettled weather festered over southeast Ohio on July 17th and 18th in the midst of hot and muggy conditions. On the 17th, two rounds of thunderstorms swept through the area, leading to downed trees across Athens, Meigs, and Lawrence Counties.||On the next day, an upper level disturbance provided additional support for strong to severe thunderstorms. In the span of an hour, downed trees occurred from strong winds across Lawrence, Vinton, and Meigs Counties. A strong downburst took place in Meigs County, leading to approximately 70 knot winds in several areas. This resulted in primarily tree damage in the eastern half of the county over into parts of West Virginia.
episodes.181383: Scattered showers and thunderstorms west of the Laramie Range on the afternoon of the 17th resulted in strong downburst winds, especially over Carbon County near Interstate 80 and the North Snowy Range Foothills.
episodes.181431: An isolated severe storm moved southeast across the Ozark foothills of southeast Missouri. The storm occurred ahead of a cold front that trailed southwest from the Great Lakes across central Missouri.
episodes.181433: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms over the Ozark foothills gradually organized into a small complex of thunderstorms as they moved east into the Mississippi Valley. Sporadic damaging wind gusts and large hail accompanied the strongest storms. The storms occurred ahead of a cold front that trailed southwest from the Great Lakes across central Missouri.
episodes.181650: A broken line of storms moved over southern Lake Michigan late in the evening of July 16th into the early morning hours on July 17th.
episodes.181749: A cold front combined with strong upper level dynamics and instability to produce scattered strong to marginally severe thunderstorms during the early evening hours on Sunday (7/16).  The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size and damaging winds.
episodes.181862: The passage of a weak cold front and upper level disturbance let to numerous strong thunderstorms across southern WI One storm became severe via downburst winds in the Lake Wisconsin area.
episodes.181914: Broad troughing was in the low and mid levels across the region with prevailing SW flow and above normal moisture content over the local area. High DCAPE over 1000 J/kg favored wet downbursts in stronger cells.
episodes.181915: Broad troughing was in the low and mid-levels across the region with prevailing SW flow and above normal moisture content over the local area. High DCAPE over 1000 J/kg favored wet downbursts in stronger cells.
episodes.181916: Broad troughing was in the low and mid-levels across the region with prevailing SW flow and above normal moisture content over the local area. High DCAPE over 1000 J/kg favored wet downbursts in stronger cells.
episodes.181992: A deep longwave trough, south-southwest flow at all levels, and the development of a QLCS (quasi-linear convective system) created all the ingredients for a widespread and susbstantial flash flood event across much of southern New England.  For a few hours during the late morning, helicity values were high and a brief tornado formed along the QLCS in North Brookfield, MA.
episodes.182101: Convection developed in west central Iowa shortly after midnight on July 17th, developing on the nose of mid level theta-e advection and associated surface front lagging behind. Despite the timing, the environment recovered thanks to continued warm air advection, effective CAPE of over 1700 J/kg, and deep layer shear over 50 kts. Storms refired around 5 am, producing up to quarter sized hail as cells moved across southern Iowa through mid morning.
episodes.182129: Two rounds of scattered thunderstorms occurred on July 17th as a cold front moved through central Illinois. The first round of thunderstorms occurred during the early afternoon, and then additional development occurred during the evening. Both rounds of thunderstorms produced large hail, primarily near or just south of the I-72 corridor.
episodes.182144: A thunderstorm became severe over northern Campbell County, producing very large hail north of Gillette.
episodes.182251: On the evening of July 15th isolated thunderstorms developed across southern New Hampshire.  Storm movement mitigated flash flooding across the state, except for the city of Manchester where multiple storms traveled directly over the city on the evening of July 15th.  Up to 2��� fell in an hour over the urban city area.  The intense rainfall rates lead to rapid run-off and caused localized urban street flooding with water due to run-off entering some building structures.  Lighter showers passed across the area later in the evening before rain ended.||On July 16th a more widespread area of rain impacted most of the state.  Rain showers began to develop around daybreak on July 16th and quickly became more widespread during the morning hours.  Light to moderate rainfall became widespread across the state with embedded bands of heavy rain.  Locally heavy rainfall continued straight through the morning hours into early afternoon on the 16th before rainfall intensity and coverage began to decrease.  Central and Southern New Hampshire received the heaviest rainfall through the day, with less rainfall across the Connecticut River Valley and the Seacoast.  Rainfall amounts of 2+��� were widespread across Central New Hampshire with two corridors of locally heavier rain in this area.  One corridor of heavy rain was from eastern Cheshire County through northwest Hillsborough County and into Central Merrimack County.  Observed reports of 3+��� of rain occurred in this region with one localized report of 4+���.  The heavy rain caused isolated areas of flooded roads along with wash-outs in Antrim where a localized area of heavy rain occurred.  The second corridor of heavy rain across the state was the most significant for the event.  This corridor of rain ran from the Massachusetts border around Nashua all the way to the Maine border in southern Carroll County.  There were numerous reports of 3+��� of rain with localized areas receiving over 4��� of rainfall by early afternoon.  The majority of this rainfall fell in a 3 to 4 hour window in the late morning hours.  The heavy rainfall rates and saturated grounds led to rapid run-off of small streams and creeks which led to flash flooding.  Flash flooding was considerable in the Barnstead, Alton and Wolfeboro region where numerous roads were closed due to severe flooding and wash-outs.  Additional urban flash flooding also occurred in the Manchester area due to flooded roads.  Minor property flooding was also reported on numerous lakefronts across the region due to very high lake levels after this rain event.   ||Localized river flooding also occurred in response to the July 15-16th rainfall with river flooding beginning on July 16th and lasting through the 18th, with river crests occurring on July 17th.  The Warner River touched minor flood stage with no significant impacts.  The Suncook River crested at 3.53ft above flood stage on July 17th.  This led to flooding of campgrounds along the river that caused the evacuation of at least one located in the floodplain. All rivers dropped below flood stage on July 18th.||In addition to the flooding, the environment supported a conditional threat for severe weather as the abundant low level moisture and strong low level jet caused significant low level shear.  This caused for numerous storms to have rotation with them that triggered tornado warnings but no tornadoes were confirmed.  There was however some localized tree damage with the associated thunderstorms across Southern New Hampshire.
episodes.182272: An upper level trough was centered over the Great Lakes region and an upper level ridge was centered over Arizona and New Mexico. South central and central Nebraska were on the backside of the upper trough. The edge of a cooler airmass was moving across central Nebraska and an upper disturbance was moving near the area. This had provided enhanced lift in the atmosphere. The air was moist with dewpoints in the 60s. Most unstable CAPE values were generally 2,000+ J/kg across the area, and zero to six km wind shear values were 50+ knots. ||Storms were developing across south central and central Nebraska during the early morning hours. One of these storms developed and strengthened to the west and moved eastward towards Merrick County. This storm produced an estimated 70 mph wind gust at 4:55 AM CDT which damaged trees, a home, and a power pole.
episodes.182342: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.182481: Wind damage resulted from an isolated severe storm in Muskegon county.
episodes.182644: An upper level storm system moved into Virginia late in the evening and with enough instability in place, a few scattered storms developed. One of the storms became severe, producing pockets of damaging winds across the New River Valley.
episodes.182699: Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall trained across portions of northern VT during the evening of July 16 dropping two to four inches of rain in some areas.
episodes.182773: Elevated storms developed in a deep shear environment and produced severe hail ranging between 1 to 1.75 inches during the morning hours.
episodes.182774: Elevated storms developed in a deep shear environment and produced severe hail ranging between 1 to 1.5 inches during the morning hours.
episodes.182998: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.  In addition, weak steering flow resulted in some slow moving storms with reports of flash flooding, particularly in Jackson and Walton counties.
episodes.183007: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.183115: Thunderstorms intensified as they moved southeast across southeastern Kansas during the morning of the 17th. These storms moved into northeastern Oklahoma during the early afternoon. The atmosphere ahead of the storms became very unstable, and wind shear was strong, which supported well-organized severe thunderstorms, including a few supercells. The strongest storms produced hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183116: Thunderstorms intensified as they moved southeast across southeastern Kansas during the morning of the 17th. These storms moved across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183171: With the influence of a mid-level trough to the north, South Florida was provided with a source of lift, which combined with surface instability from diurnal heating to develop strong to severe thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 17th.
episodes.183237: A modest push of monsoon moisture and ongoing extreme heat fueled spotty thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Isolated high winds and flash flooding occurred.
episodes.183290: Isolated supercells moved southeast across the panhandle and Sandhills during the evening hours of July 16, resulting in multiple reports of large hail, some significant, and damaging winds.
episodes.183312: A series of short waves moved across there region and interacted with the very hot and moist air mass that had been in place. Thunderstorms moved front the northwest to the southeast across the region and several became severe.
episodes.183329: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and moved northwest across southeast Arizona through the evening. Storms produced damaging winds and large hail across eastern Pima County and the Tohono O'odham Nation and a dust storm in Pinal County. The Catalina Foothills were especially hit hard with numerous power poles downed leaving thousands without power for two days.
episodes.183336: A short wave moved across the region spawning multiple severe storms in Southwest Louisiana, however only one storm became severe in Southeast Texas.
episodes.183346: Perhaps the most impactful severe weather in July spread from northwest into central and southeast sections of the state on the 14th/15th. Two to more than three inches of rain fell from Fort Smith (Sebastian County) to Waldron (Scott County) and Mena (Polk County). ||Little Rock National Airport (Pulaski County) had a gust of 58 mph. A tree fell on a camping vehicle at Diamond City (Boone County), and a barn was overturned near Whiteville (Baxter County). Trees were toppled near Fairview (Ouachita County).||There were spotty instances of hail/damaging wind across the northern and central counties on the 17th/18th.
episodes.183479: A shift in the atmospheric pattern from mid to late July brought an array of impacts to much of Utah, including severe thunderstorm wind gusts, large hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.183534: Storms occurred from the early afternoon to the evening of the 17th ahead of the southward moving cold front. The storms mainly affected locations along and east of a line from Stockton to Springfield to Branson, and produced hail up to 3 inches in diameter at Preston in Hickory County. Wind damage and wind gusts over 70 mph were also reported. The town of Theodosia in Ozark County was especially hard hit with widespread tree damage. Rainfall accumulations averaged between one to two inches, with isolated accumulations over three inches in Laclede and Camden counties.
episodes.183637: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the early afternoon hours on the southeast Georgia coast. One thunderstorm became strong enough to produce strong wind gusts on Sapelo Island.
episodes.183719: Thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds across western Kansas.
episodes.183722: Large hail and damaging winds were reported across western Kansas.
episodes.183744: A complex of storms developed near Interstate 70 and quickly intensified as it progressed southeastward into the Flint Hills. A swath of large hail and damaging winds impacted along and just east of the Flint Hills with the first round of storms during the late morning and early afternoon hours. Then a second round of storms developed across Greenwood and Elk counties and quickly intensified. These storms also produced large hail and damaging winds across the same areas that were impacted by the first round of storms.
episodes.183842: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours on the sea breeze along the southeast Georgia coast. One thunderstorm produced frequent lightning, striking a building in Savannah.
episodes.183847: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.183925: On the afternoon of July 17th, a supercell developed near Grandview and moved to the southeast through Raymore, Harrisonville, Garden City, and continued on into WFO Springfield's area. This supercell produced very large hail, including a 5 hail stone near Garden City.
episodes.184169: A very strong area of high pressure that brought record heat to northern Arizona in the previous few days started to move eastward. This allowed a southerly flow to develop over the area transporting moisture northward from Mexico. This moisture allowed for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms over parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.184387: An upper level high pressure center was located over central Arizona and central New Mexico which resulted in a favorable pattern for efficient diurnal wind fluctuations including upslope oriented winds towards WFO Pueblo's eastern mountains. Weak waves embedded in the upper level northwesterly flow enhanced the lift and the pattern enhanced the deep shear. The result was a very rare mountainous tornado that was observed at around 9,000 feet.
episodes.184453: Storms developed just south of the I-70 corridor during the early morning hours of July 17th. With precipitable water values between 1.5 and 2.0 inches and the storms oriented in a west to east line, training caused heavy rainfall in some isolated areas with 1 to 3 inches (very localized 4 to 5 inches) of rain. So there were reports of flash flooding in a few locations.
episodes.184457: An outflow boundary in the vicinity of I-70 was the focus of thunderstorm development. The air mass along and south of this boundary was quite unstable with surface based CAPE of 3500+ J/kg with decent convergence. There were numerous reports of large hail and some damaging winds.
episodes.184458: An outflow boundary in the vicinity of I-70 was the focus of thunderstorm development. The air mass along and south of this boundary was quite unstable with surface based CAPE of 3500+ J/kg with decent convergence. There were numerous reports of large hail and some damaging winds.
